## Root cause

`/click/src/click/core.py`, `Option.__init__` (old lines 2519-2520):

```python
if is_flag and default_is_missing:
    self.default: t.Union[t.Any, t.Callable[[], t.Any]] = False
```

When `is_flag=True` and no `default=` was passed, Click *forced* `self.default = False`. That implicit default then defeated the `required` check:

* `Parameter.consume_value` (core.py:2253-2255) falls back to `self.get_default(ctx)` → `False`, source `DEFAULT`.
* `Parameter.process_value` (core.py:2318-2322) only raises `MissingParameter` when `self.value_is_missing(value)` (core.py:2309-2316), which returns True only for `None` (or `()` when `multiple`/`nargs != 1`). `False` is not "missing", so `required=True` was silently ignored.
* The same default also feeds `flag_value = not self.default` and the guessed type, so the flag behaved as a normal optional bool flag.

## Diff applied (`git diff`)

```diff
--- a/src/click/core.py
+++ b/src/click/core.py
@@ -2516,8 +2516,10 @@ class Option(Parameter):
             # flag if flag_value is set.
             self._flag_needs_value = flag_value is not None
 
-        if is_flag and default_is_missing:
-            self.default: t.Union[t.Any, t.Callable[[], t.Any]] = False
+        self.default: t.Union[t.Any, t.Callable[[], t.Any]]
+
+        if is_flag and default_is_missing and not self.required:
+            self.default = False
 
         if flag_value is None:
             flag_value = not self.default
```

Now a required flag keeps `default = None`, so `consume_value` returns `None` → `value_is_missing(None)` → `MissingParameter` (a `UsageError`, exit code 2). The annotation was moved to its own line because the assignment is now conditional (matches upstream style). Only `/click/src/click/core.py` was modified; no tests touched.

## Reproduction (scripts in /tmp/repro, click imported from /click/src)

r1 = `@click.option("--on/--off", is_flag=True, required=True)`; r2 = `("--on/--off", default=False, required=True)`;
